selected_evidence.requirement: Inventory application served over TCP 8181 on node1
selected_evidence.summary: httpd configured to Listen 8181, serving /var/www/html/index.html inventory table; curl returns HTTP 200 with inventory content and ss shows httpd listening on 8181

selected_evidence.requirement: SELinux (mandatory access control) remains in enforcing mode while the service runs on the non-default port
selected_evidence.summary: getenforce reports Enforcing before, during, and after setup; port 8181 was explicitly relabeled http_port_t via semanage so httpd could bind it under SELinux, and no AVC denials were logged for httpd
Captured boot_id 910dc564-cb62-46fc-8290-c332e63d6201, SELinux Enforcing, httpd active, port 8181 listening, app returning HTTP 200
systemd-run --on-active=1 --no-block scheduled systemctl reboot and returned confirmation immediately, prior to the node going down

selected_evidence.requirement: Proof of actual restart via changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Node became unreachable (connection reset/timeout) confirming the reboot took effect, then came back reachable with boot_id e7f748e9-2412-4002-b295-433f9a13f883, differing from the pre-restart boot_id

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services, data, and SELinux enforcement
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot: SELinux still Enforcing, httpd active and enabled (auto-started), port 8181 listening and firewalld-open, http_port_t label intact, curl to inventory app returns HTTP 200 with correct content, no AVC denials
